pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:741 tools/call dispatches through a hand-written match over tool names that is maintained separately from the server_tools listing, and nothing at this door reads a caller principal or scope: tools are gated only by global config switches, so the door neither resolves through one registry nor authorizes per caller.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:72 The door treats every non-job-token caller as anonymous. Off-context, auth::required_scope classifies every POST /mcp as Admin in keys mode (and admits it unauthenticated in the default open mode). The existing enqueue:<app>/read scopes never decide which tools resolve, so a read key cannot even list and per-tool scoping from the key registry is not realized.

crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:746 The gating predicate is restated in both server_tools (listing) and the dispatch match: two authorities for 'what exists'. The validator does read the listing's schema (good), but there is no registry entry carrying handler+scope, no door-level audit line, and panics are caught only by the HTTP-wide CatchPanicLayer (whole response 500, not an in-band isError).

crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:61 Streamable HTTP on a local port (default host 127.0.0.1 in config.rs). No Origin validation was found anywhere in mcp/ or auth.rs, and the token requirement is opt-in ([auth] mode defaults to open), so enabling MCP alone ships an unauthenticated localhost listener. The technique requires these checks to be on unless deliberately removed.

crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:731 The published inputSchema is the enforced artifact at one door; schema violations are in-band isError results and an unknown tool is a protocol error. Residual: bare verb names 'search'/'fetch' are not namespaced (hosts usually prefix them).
crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:1656 The agent fetch surface subtracts exactly the strategy that breaks the no-recursion invariant and refuses it by name, naming this tool as the surface.
crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:1412 approve_transaction requires the digest of the evidence the agent actually read, checked by approve_decision before the irreversible write.
crates/server/src/mcp/live.rs:262 wait_job has one clamped wall-clock budget and returns timed_out with the current snapshot rather than an empty success; wait_workflow mirrors it.
crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:891 The `$.path:op:value` filter notation is parsed by the server's own parser with a closed op set (eq|contains|gte|lte|numgte), shared with the HTTP surface.

crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:75 The product's own Claude subprocess reaches the tools through the same POST /mcp door, presenting a job token as a header; there is no in-process side door to the handlers.
crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:150 The server fronts a service, not a single-seat interactive application; no argument names a current selection.
crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:29 No affinity or session routing exists; POST is stateless and the SSE feed is not a session.

crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:332 Half-finished work lives in the server's durable store (checkpoint); the caller carries only a job id, so there is no caller-carried continuation to seal. The job id is not bound to a principal, which matters only once per-caller scoping exists.

pairs.registryProposal: authentication-and-scoping could name the 'whole endpoint behind one coarse scope' shape (here every POST to the tool endpoint demands admin): it is closed rather than open, yet it still fails per-tool scoping and makes listing require the strongest grant. That is a distinct failure from the unauthenticated door.
